html:
The Warsaw Ghetto Uprising was a revolt by Jews in the Warsaw Ghetto against German troops sent to deport its last inhabitants, which began on 19 April 1943 and was crushed by 16 May.

The ghetto had held some 400,000 Jews behind walls from 1940, and in 1942 the Germans sent about 265,000 of them to their deaths at Treblinka. The young fighters of the Jewish Combat Organisation, led by Mordechai Anielewicz, and another group fought with pistols and homemade bombs. The Germans burned the ghetto block by block. Anielewicz died in his bunker on 8 May. The German commander blew up the Great Synagogue to mark the end. It was the largest Jewish revolt of the Holocaust. In 1970 West German chancellor Willy Brandt knelt at its memorial. A year later the city rose again in the Warsaw Uprising.
sum: The Warsaw Ghetto Uprising was a revolt by Jews in the Warsaw Ghetto against German troops sent to deport its last inhabitants, which began on 19 April 1943 and was crushed by 16 May.
